distinguishing_features: Passive Thermal-Mass Suction Line Decoupling using existing copper piping as a thermal buffer
Prevention of liquid slugging via thermodynamic inertia instead of flow restriction or active control
Exploitation of volumetric heat capacity of the suction line to maintain superheat during startup transients
Modification limited to increased insulation on a segment of existing suction line without new hardware or valves
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent liquid refrigerant from reaching the orbiting scroll during compressor startup under cold ambient conditions without adding active components or flow-restricting devices
parsed.viable_reason: The thermal mass of copper and insulated refrigerant line can realistically maintain superheat for the duration of a typical startup transient based on standard heat transfer calculations.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The use of inherent thermal inertia of the suction line as a protective mechanism against slugging is not an obvious extension of prior art, which focuses on active sensing, flow manipulation, or mechanical separation rather than passive thermodynamic decoupling.
